minutes.headline: Committee to revise its proposed bylaw so the select board appoints members, targeting the March 16 town meeting warrant
minutes.summary: The Open Space Committee approved prior minutes and spent most of the meeting on its draft enabling bylaw, discussing town counsel's recommendation to shift appointing authority from the planning board to the select board and simplifying how other boards' representatives join the committee. No formal votes were taken on the bylaw itself; the chair planned to present a revised draft to the town's bylaw review committee the next evening ahead of the March 16 warrant deadline, and the committee also heard routine reports from conservation, parks, and the EDC.

what_happened.line: The committee will revise its draft bylaw so the select board, not the planning board, appoints its members, on town counsel's advice.
Representatives from other boards -- planning, conservation, agriculture, parks -- would be appointed directly by their own boards rather than needing a second, separate appointment.
If the agriculture commission does not name a representative, that seat becomes at-large, a question set for the March 11 meeting.
The town meeting warrant article will be filed as a placeholder, with final bylaw wording to follow closer to the March 16 deadline.
No vote was taken on the bylaw itself; the chair plans to bring a revised draft to the bylaw review committee the next evening.

why_it_matters: This bylaw, if it reaches the March 16 town meeting warrant, is what residents would vote to create the Open Space Committee under and to set who appoints its members.
Moving appointing authority to the select board changes which elected body residents hold accountable for who sits on the committee.
Whether the agriculture commission gets a dedicated seat or the seat goes at-large affects who represents farming interests on open-space decisions.
